# a11y-agent-kit

> The Bring Your Own Agent (BYOA) MVP for local accessibility auditing is available on npm as `a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2`. It audits your running app or any HTTP(S) site you are authorized to test. Your coding agent explores rendered browser states with Playwright and axe, saves evidence and checkpoints, and produces HTML reports that label findings awaiting review. The audit workflow collects evidence. The kit has no model service, account, or report upload.

## Install and start

- Use Node.js 22.12+ and npm.
- From the app's project root, run `npx -y a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2 init --install --write`. It writes `evidence/audit-manifest.json`, downloads the matching Chromium from the Playwright CDN if it is missing, and creates MCP settings for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex where none exist. It never changes an existing MCP configuration file. Without `init`, install the matching Chromium with `npx -y playwright@1.64.1 install chromium`.
- Run `npx -y a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2` with the documented subcommand and arguments. See the [first audit command](README.md#run-your-first-audit-from-npm) and [agent prompt](README.md#copy-this-to-your-agent).
- For a global installation, run `npm install -g a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2` and use `a11y-agent-kit` with the same subcommands. For a local stdio MCP host, configure `npx -y a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2 serve`. See [MCP configuration](examples/byoa-audit.md#mcp-connection).

## Skills

- [a11y-audit](skills/a11y-audit/SKILL.md) covers evidence collection, checkpoints, submission, separate review, and HTML delivery. Read the [current copy](https://github.com/szboynono/a11y-agent-kit/blob/main/skills/a11y-audit/SKILL.md).
- [a11y-fix-loop](skills/a11y-fix-loop/SKILL.md) covers the historical, limited analyze/edit/verify/check workflow for button-name, label, and aria-valid-attr.

## Use and output

1. Use the target's HTTP(S) URL and a canonical absolute `projectRoot` in `evidence/audit-manifest.json`: your app's project root for your own app, or a dedicated, empty workspace for a deployed or third-party site you are authorized to test. For a remote site, resolve the canonical start URL first; main-document navigation stays on the manifest origin. The kit does not crawl, sign in or bypass bot protection. See the [remote-site guide](examples/remote-site.md). New audits support WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 at level A or AA. The default is 2.2 AA.
2. Start one persistent JSONL process with `npx -y a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2 audit-agent evidence/audit-manifest.json`. Run snapshot and axe, adopt bound candidates, and explore relevant states. Read original records and view PNGs before making visual claims. Save checkpoints, then explicitly submit the last acknowledged digest. Use fixed batch collection if the host cannot keep a process open.
3. Run `npx -y a11y-agent-kit@0.1.2 audit-report REPORT.json --out evidence/a11y-report.html` with the returned checkpoint, proposal, or reviewed report JSON. Use `--screenshots` only with permission to embed page pixels.
4. Return the HTML and original artifact paths, counts by status, unresolved observations, and untested scope. Submissions stay `needs_review` pending separate review. Use `audit-check` to check integrity and source freshness.

WCAG conformance and real screen-reader speech remain unassessed. Evidence uses absolute, source-bound paths. Keep the original project and evidence tree. The browser and the host agent may use the network. The host controls what captured text, URLs, and pixels reach its model.
